column1: # Single source of truth for toolchain and service versions.
# Every version literal in templates/, tooling/, tests/, and .github/ must agree
# with the value here. version_consistency_check.sh proves it.
# class decides whether Foundation may move a scaffolded app forward on its own:
#   reversible    Reverting costs a version-number change and nothing else. No
#                 state is written that a downgrade cannot read. Foundation may
#                 bump these for apps; a customized value only warns.
#   irreversible  Reverting requires restoring from backup, because upgrading
#                 rewrites on-disk state (pg_upgrade, RDB/AOF format). Foundation
#                 must NEVER bump these for an app. A customized value fails.
# supported is what an app is allowed to be on, not what Foundation ships:
#   current       The app must match value exactly. Used for reversible things,
#                 where there is no cost to staying current.
#   MIN..MAX      The app may sit anywhere in the inclusive range. Used for
#                 irreversible things, so a 2027 app can still be supported in
#                 2035 without being force-migrated. `value` is what a NEW app is
#                 seeded with; existing apps are only checked against the range.
#   any           Foundation seeds a default and never checks or moves it.
# Bumping an irreversible MIN is a breaking change for apps below it and needs a
# migration note in CHANGELOG.md.
# Distributions vs versions. A project may run PostGIS, TimescaleDB, pgvector, or
# Valkey instead of the stock image. That choice is the project's and Foundation
# does not constrain it — hence the *_IMAGE keys with `any`. What Foundation does
# constrain is the ENGINE MAJOR, because that is what decides whether an existing
# data directory can be read. So POSTGRES_VERSION=16-3.4 (PostGIS on Postgres 16)
# is range-checked as 16, and only the leading integer is compared.
# key
GO_VERSION
column5: Go toolchain for builds and CI; wrapper substrate, no persisted state.

column1: NODE_VERSION
column5: Node for frontend build and CI.

column1: ALPINE_VERSION
column5: Base image for Go build and runtime stages.

column1: MIGRATE_VERSION
column5: golang-migrate CLI image; the tool is stateless, the migrations it applies are not.

column1: POSTGRES_BASE_IMAGE
POSTGRES_VERSION
column5: Major version upgrade rewrites the data directory (pg_upgrade). Range-checked on the leading engine major, so 16-3.4 reads as 16.

column1: REDIS_BASE_IMAGE
REDIS_VERSION
column5: RDB/AOF format is not downgrade-safe once written. Range-checked on the leading major.
